title: Ergothioneine: skin benefits, interactions, and usage - HealthWithFacts
abstract:
## What is ergothioneine  
Ergothioneine is a special type of amino acid that your body cannot make on its own – you must get it from food. Think of it as nature’s own protective shield that certain organisms create to survive harsh conditions. This water-soluble compound is primarily found in mushrooms, which act like little factories producing this valuable ingredient [1](javascript:void%280%29)Halliwell, B., Cheah, I. K., & Tang, R. M. Y. (2018). Ergothioneine–a diet‐derived antioxidant with therapeutic potential. FEBS letters, 592(20), 3357-3366..  
What makes ergothioneine truly special is that your body has evolved a specific “door” or transporter called OCTN1 that actively seeks out and brings this compound into your cells. This selective transporter acts like a VIP pass, allowing ergothioneine to enter cells where it’s needed most [2](javascript:void%280%29)Paul, B. D., & Snyder, S. H. (2010). The unusual amino acid L-ergothioneine is a physiologic cytoprotectant. Cell Death & Differentiation, 17(7), 1134-1140.. The fact that we evolved this special transport system suggests ergothioneine must be incredibly important for our health.
## Natural sources of ergothioneine  
The best natural sources of ergothioneine are mushrooms – nature’s powerhouses for this protective compound. Different mushroom varieties contain varying amounts, with some being particularly rich sources:  
**Highest ergothioneine content mushrooms:**  
- King oyster mushrooms
- Shiitake mushrooms
- Maitake mushrooms
- Oyster mushrooms  
One serving of mushrooms can contain 2.4 to 4.9mg of ergothioneine, with oyster mushrooms containing approximately 10 times more ergothioneine than most other dietary sources [3](javascript:void%280%29)Beelman, R. B., Kalaras, M. D., & Phillips, A. T. (2019). Is ergothioneine a ‘longevity vitamin’ limited in the American diet? Journal of nutritional science, 8. [4](javascript:void%280%29)Kalaras, M. D., Richie, J. P., Calcagnotto, A., & Beelman, R. B. (2017). Mushrooms: A rich source of the antioxidants ergothioneine and glutathione. Food chemistry, 233, 429-433..  
You can also find smaller amounts in black beans, red beans, and oat bran. Interestingly, animals that eat grasses containing ergothioneine (like grass-fed livestock) also contain this compound in their organs [5](javascript:void%280%29)WebMD. (n.d.). ERGOTHIONEINE: Overview, Uses, Side Effects, Precautions, Interactions, Dosing and Reviews..
## How ergothioneine works on the skin  
### The OCTN1 transport system  
Your skin cells have that same special transporter (OCTN1) that actively pulls ergothioneine where it’s needed most. Research shows that skin cells not only have this transporter but actually depend on it to fight damage from UV light and environmental stress [6](javascript:void%280%29)Guo, C., Wei, J., Yang, J., Xu, J., Pang, W., & Jiang, Y. (2008). Pomegranate juice is potentially better than apple juice in improving antioxidant function in elderly subjects. Nutrition Research, 28(2), 72-77..  
Think of OCTN1 as your skin’s emergency response system – when cells are under attack from sun damage or pollution, this transporter rushes ergothioneine to those areas to provide protection and help with repair.
